output.narrative_summary: This result rests on the link from Competitive Intensity to Revenue Growth. If competition intensifies further, more runs could support a different option. In this model, 72% of runs supported Enter European Market.

story_headlines.opt_expand: Enter European Market benefits from a positive link from market entry through to revenue growth in this model.
story_headlines.opt_wait: Delay to Next Year would need competitive intensity to rise substantially before more runs support it.

robustness_explanation.summary: The ordering holds in about 91% of variations, based on current estimates.
robustness_explanation.primary_risk: The link from Competitive Intensity to Revenue Growth is the main relationship that could shift this comparison.
stability_factors: Europe Market Entry shows a well evidenced positive link to Revenue Growth.
Pricing Power adds a further positive link to Revenue Growth.
fragility_factors: The link from Competitive Intensity to Revenue Growth could flip the comparison if intensity rises.

output.readiness_rationale: The comparison is settled on your numbers: Europe Market Entry and Pricing Power both support Enter European Market, with only competitive intensity as an open question worth a quick check.

fac_competition.specific_action: Commission a short competitor scan of the target European segment covering active entrants and pricing moves.
fac_competition.rationale: Competitive Intensity is the one relationship that could change which option more runs support.
fac_competition.decision_hygiene: Estimate the current level of competitive intensity before reviewing the scan.

edge_competition_revenue.trigger_description: If the link from Competitive Intensity to Revenue Growth strengthens as rivals respond to entry...
edge_competition_revenue.consequence: ...then the most runs would support Delay to Next Year rather than Enter European Market.

flip_thresholds.narrative: If Competitive Intensity moves from 35% to 62%, more runs would support a different option.

key_assumptions: The link from Europe Market Entry to Revenue Growth assumes current market conditions hold through launch.
The brief's goal of reaching eight hundred pro customers assumes the four hundred baseline stays stable during expansion.
The link from Pricing Power to Revenue Growth assumes pricing can be maintained once competitors respond.

decision_quality_prompts.question: What would make you switch to Delay to Next Year?
decision_quality_prompts.applies_because: The comparison is well supported for Enter European Market, so it is worth naming what specifically would reverse that.

decision_quality_prompts.question: This failed because competitive intensity in the European market rose sharply after entry, what signs would have shown this coming?
decision_quality_prompts.applies_because: The comparison is settled enough to act on, but the link from Competitive Intensity to Revenue Growth is the one open fragility worth stress-testing in advance.

pre_mortem.failure_scenario: Enter European Market failed because Competitive Intensity rose faster than expected, eroding the positive link from Europe Market Entry to Revenue Growth.
warning_signs: New entrants or price cuts appearing in the target European segment ahead of launch.
Early pricing power softening faster than planned in initial European accounts.
pre_mortem.mitigation: Run the competitor scan before committing full launch resources.
pre_mortem.review_trigger: Reconvene if competitive intensity signals increase before launch.
